headline: Shift Grid Costs to Large Energy Users
short_summary: This bill aims to shift certain grid infrastructure and capacity costs from residential ratepayers to large energy users, including data centers, potentially lowering residential utility bills.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP1123) on 2026-05-14
supporters: Residential consumer groups, Governor Spanberger's administration, State Corporation Commission (SCC), Dominion Energy (initially).
opponents: Large energy users (data centers, large manufacturers).
news_headline: Virginia Requires Data Centers to Pay for New Transmission
news_summary: Governor Spanberger urged the SCC to make data centers cover the cost of transmission infrastructure built exclusively for them, saving residential ratepayers hundreds of millions. This order ensures data centers pay the full cost of their required transmission infrastructure.

headline: Mandatory Data Center Water Use Reporting
short_summary: This bill mandates water suppliers to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency regarding their water consumption.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, water conservation advocates, local communities, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
news_headline: New Regulations Beef Up Data Centers' Water Reporting
news_summary: New regulations taking effect in January will provide more insight into data center water usage in Virginia, though specific facility data remains protected. The law requires waterworks operators to categorize monthly sales data, including usage by data centers, to fill a data gap for environmental planning.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Assessments
short_summary: This bill requires site assessments for new high energy use facilities, including noise studies for nearby residential areas and schools, and allows localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local communities, residents near data center sites, environmental groups, Delegate Joshua Thomas.
opponents: Data center developers, real estate interests.
news_headline: Manassas Tightens Data Center Zoning Rules
news_summary: Manassas City Council unanimously approved stricter zoning rules for data centers, requiring pre-construction noise studies and strengthening architectural design. These changes address resident complaints about noise and visual impact, formalizing requirements previously negotiated with developers.
